title: The 2 am Call
logline: The groom takes the bride's left hand and starts sliding the bangles off one by one. She stops him by lifting the drugged milk to her own lips and gives him a false name to chase. He tells her calmly what he will do to the woman whose hand is in his photograph, and promises 'Sneha' she can walk. At 2 am Mausi rings on speaker and asks whether the son-in-law has drunk his milk.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; Mausi, beta, Damaad ji, mathri and the names kept as spoken in India.
script_note: Indian English in Latin script, adapted from script.hi.json (not translated); same cast, beats, line ids and speakers.

characters.name: Kiran
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride, here as 'Sneha'. Since the middle of s1e01 she talks to Aditya as Kiran: low, flat, quick.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Wheat-brown skin, oval face, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, a closed, watchful mouth. Low bun, centre parting with sindoor, small round red bindi, thin plain gold ring in the LEFT nostril, small gold studs, short black-bead mangalsutra. Plain sindoor-red matte saree with a thin plain gold border, red elbow-sleeve blouse, pallu over the left shoulder, barefoot. Old-style block henna on both hands (a solid disc in each palm, fingertips dipped). Red-and-ivory chooda on both forearms, reading as a red cuff about 10 cm long with a pale band at each end. The scar on her left forearm is never in frame in this episode.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge. Small-city Madhya Pradesh Indian English, learnt at school and from a phone: simple, quick, with contractions, a light Hindi accent, no British or American colour. Keeps Mausi. To Aditya she is Kiran: lower, flat, quick, short sentences. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill. Lies come out easily (l05 to l07, l11); true things come after a pause (l12, l20).

characters.name: Aditya
characters.role: The groom: a pharmacist who made himself the gang's mark to reach Mausi and the bride who robbed his brother.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow, a slight stoop. Light-brown skin, long clean-shaven face, neat left-parted black hair, rimless rectangular glasses in every shot. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta with a band collar and sleeves folded back once, cream churidar, barefoot. A brass key about 5 cm long on a doubled red thread round his neck, outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch on a brown strap, never readable.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken. Careful small-city Madhya Pradesh Indian English, a science graduate's: complete sentences, few contractions, precise nouns (dose, code, ledger, police), a clear Indian accent, no British or American colour. Even and unhurried, almost courteous, like a man reading out a prescription. Under pressure he slows down and drops in volume; he never shouts. The one place the voice may catch is his brother's name (l14, l18).

characters.name: Shakun Mausi
characters.role: Runs the bureau and the brides; the only mother Kiran has had. Voice only in this episode.
characters.look: Not seen in this episode (production lock). A voice on Billu's phone in the lane (b9) and on Kiran's phone on speaker (b10, b13).
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, mid 50s, low, warm and grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Warm, motherly Indian English with a strong Bundelkhand Hindi accent, short plain sentences, Hindi endearments kept (beta, Damaad ji); she sounds like someone's aunt at a wedding. No British or American colour. Laughs easily. She never raises her voice; the colder the decision, the softer and slower she gets. On the phone she is fully voiced and clear, never a whisper. On this call she says beta and never the name.

characters.name: Billu
characters.role: The bride's 'brother', driver and lookout, waiting in the lane.
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry and restless. Brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, black hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket with the sleeves pushed up over a black T-shirt, dark jeans, grey-white sneakers. A wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth and a car key on a steel ring hooked on his right index finger. No weapon.
characters.voice_note: No lines in this episode (l26 cut after critic round 1); his grin in b9 carries it. For the series: same actor, quick, slangy small-town Indian English with a Bundelkhand accent, an article dropped now and then; keeps Jijaji, Mausi, arre. Never American street slang.

characters.name: The boys
characters.look: Never a face. Two fixed backlit shapes by the motorbike: one heavy-set with a shaved head and a maroon track jacket; one thin, in a checked shirt and a cloth cap. Backs, hands and silhouettes only, heads cropped, turned away or in full shadow.

location: The bridal bedroom on the first floor of a rented house in a small Madhya Pradesh city (b1 to b7, b10, b13), and the empty lane below it with Billu's parked car (b9, b12).
time_of_day: Night 1, late April, about 1:45 to 2:00 am. Warm night, window shutters open.

beats.action: Opens in the same second s1e01 ended; the print is still raised. Set-up 1 (l01, inside the first 2 s): two-shot across the room's width in warm lamp light, as s1e01 left them: Aditya on the edge of the bed among loose marigold petals, glasses on, the brass key on its red thread at mid-chest, the creased print still raised in his right hand; Kiran at the pale-blue door, her right hand against it, pallu over her left shoulder. Set-up 2 (the silence after, 1.5 s): she has crossed to the window side of the bed, by the stool, and holds both hands out to him over the white sheet, palms up: a solid henna disc in each palm, fingertips dipped, the red cuff whole on both forearms, both cuffs at rest just above the wrist bone; she slid the right one down on her way from the door. Palms up, the outer forearms face the sheet; nothing above either cuff shows.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Show me your hands. Both.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (l02): close over the white sheet. Aditya takes her LEFT hand, the hand in the photograph, turns it back up and holds it flat on the sheet with the print laid beside it; the red cuff sits exactly where the print's scar is. He does not push the cuff. He starts sliding bangles off over her hand, one at a time, unhurried, like counting strips at his counter. Set-up 2 (the silence after; each bangle is a clink in sound, not motion): insert, same angle: three loose bangles on the sheet, two ivory and one red; the cuff barely shorter and still closed over the middle of her forearm; his fingers closed on the fourth. No frame in this beat shows the scar. Storyboard: write the scar arm's picture side for each framing (D-013).

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] One at a time. I am in no hurry.

beats.action: Set-up 1 (l03): Kiran close; her free right hand has lifted the steel glass of kesar milk from the tray on the stool to her own lips, eyes on him. Set-up 2 (l04 and the silence after): Aditya has let go of her left wrist and has the glass in his own hand, setting it back on the tray out of her reach. Her left hand is back in her lap under the fall of the pallu, cuff still on it. The three bangles lie on the sheet between them.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [flatly] It'll put me to sleep, though.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [sharply] Put it down. If you're asleep, who takes me to Mausi?

beats.action: The longest beat, seven set-ups. 1 (l05): Kiran close, offering it like a gift. 2 (l06): Aditya close, listening, the print lowered to the sheet. 3 (l07): two-shot, her phone dark on the sheet between them. 4 (l08): he picks up the three bangles himself and holds them out to her on his open palm. 5 (l09): insert, her phone on the sheet: no network, time 1:52 (both overlays). 6 (l10): insert, his fingers sliding her SIM back into the phone; the network returns (overlay). He lays the phone face up on the sheet between them. 7 (l11 and the silence after): close on her left hand low in her lap, the red bangle going back on first so the pale band is at the wrist again; the cuff complete. Nobody says the call will be on speaker.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] The one with the burnt wrist? Rekha. She does Mausi's accounts now.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [flatly] Without me, Mausi's shutter won't open for you.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] Mausi calls at two. If the phone's off, Billu comes up.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Mausi first. Rekha can wait.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] And if it is a lie, I will check the wrist myself.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] So. Is there a code?

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [calm] No code. A mother asks how her daughter is. That's all.

beats.action: 1 (l12): Kiran close, not looking at him. 2 (l13): two-shot, the steel glass on the tray between them. 3 (l14): Aditya close. 4 (l15 and the silence after): Kiran close, holding still while it lands. No image of Mohit; his death is not pictured.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [hesitant] We only take the jewellery. We never touch anyone.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [flatly] At most, if a groom wakes up, the boys slap him once.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] Nobody touched Mohit either.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Our mother's bangles. The lane laughed at him for eleven days.

beats.action: 1 (l16): Aditya close, even. 2 (l17): Kiran close. 3 (l18): Aditya tighter, the key on its red thread in frame. 4 (l19): low two-shot across the stool, the steel glass and the paper fold on the tray in the foreground. 5 (the silence after): insert under the fall of the pallu: her left hand closes into a fist over the cuff. No scar.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Mausi and her ledger go to the police. That hand does not.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [quietly] What will you do with that hand?

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Mohit lasted eleven days. She gets eleven days too. Then one dose.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] I know how much puts you to sleep, and how much means you never wake up.

beats.action: 1 (l20): Kiran close. 2 (l21, l22): Aditya close, courteous, as if this were a fair offer. 3 (the silence after): Kiran close on the name 'Sneha'. It is not hers, and her face gives nothing away.

lines.speaker: kiran
lines.text: [hesitant] And me?

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [calm] Get me to Mausi. After that, I want nothing from you.

lines.speaker: aditya
lines.text: [quietly] You are free to go, Sneha.

beats.action: Out of Aditya's hearing. 1 (the silence before, then l23): wide from the lane: Billu's old white sedan under the single sodium streetlight, the warm lit first-floor window with its iron grille above; Billu leaning on the bonnet, phone at his ear; behind the car, by the motorbike, two backlit shapes with no faces. Shutters down, nobody else, no readable sign. Mausi is a voice on Billu's phone. 2 (l24): Billu close, toothpick in the right corner of his mouth, car key on his right index finger. 3 (l25): the two shapes by the bike from behind, heads in shadow. 4 (l27): Billu close, grinning, eyes up at the window: a drill he has heard a hundred times. He says nothing.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] At two, I'll ask about the milk.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] 'He drank it', the car at three. 'The milk has split', the boys go up.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] Anything else, or silence, they still go up.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [calm] I'll see to the rest.

beats.action: 2:00 (overlay). 1 (the silence before): insert, Kiran's phone lights on the sheet between them; caller name 'Mausi' (overlay; 'मौसी' in the Hindi cut). 2 (l28, to 'Don't lie to me.'): Aditya presses speaker with one finger and lays a finger of the other hand on his own lips. 3 (l28, from 'There's mathri'): insert, his hand at the side zip pocket of the maroon bag on the wooden chair, a small round steel dabba of mathri in it; the zip is sound. 4 (l29, through the pause after 'Listen'): Aditya with the dabba in his hand, looking at it a second too long. Cut on the pause to 5 (the rest of l29): Kiran close as the question lands. On this call Mausi says beta and never the name.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [warmly] Did you eat? [chuckles] Don't lie to me. There's mathri in the side pocket of your bag.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [warmly] Listen... did Damaad ji drink his milk, beta?

beats.action: One still, no line: Billu has straightened off the bonnet, face turned up to the lit window, his hand on the car door; behind him the two shapes have straightened up from the bike. Nobody else in the lane.

1 (l30): low two-shot across the stool: the untouched steel glass on the tray in the foreground, the lit phone on the sheet, Kiran's left hand under the pallu, Aditya across the room by the chair, the steel dabba still in his hand. 2 (first half of the silence after): Aditya close, the dabba in his hand, glasses, the brass key on its red thread, his eyes on her mouth. 3 (second half): Kiran close, lips parted; she breathes in. The breath is a recorded breath or a sound effect, not a voiced line, and no word follows it. Cut to the question.

lines.speaker: mausi
lines.text: [warmly] Hello, beta? Did he drink it?

sfx_notes: Bed, bedroom beats: a warm, still small-city night through the open window: crickets, a far dog, the low hum of the sodium lamp in the lane. No fan. No music under b1 to b3.
b2: one dry glass clink for each bangle slid off over her hand and laid on the sheet (three clinks), then silence as his fingers close on the fourth.
b3: steel glass lifted from the steel tray (a small scrape), then set back down on it.
b4: a click as the SIM tray goes home; a short network chime on the phone; three soft clinks as she slides the bangles back on.
b6: the faint creak of the bed frame as he leans in for l19. Nothing under the fist insert.

b9 and b12, lane: open air, sodium-lamp buzz, a far truck on a highway. Mausi through Billu's phone: phone filter wide enough that every consonant survives; fully voiced, never a whisper. Keep all three outcomes in l24 and l25 clear above the bed.

b10: phone buzzes on the sheet twice and stops when he presses speaker (a tap). Mausi on speaker in the room: a lighter phone colour than in the lane, still fully voiced. The side-pocket zip, slow and very soft, kept well under Mausi's voice and away from the phone's pickup, so in-story she cannot hear it (a noted departure from bible b10 'without a sound': in a stills cut the pocket opening has to be heard). The lid of the steel dabba is not opened on screen.
b10 l29 and b13 l30: duck the bed and the music right down under both lines so the question and its repeat are fully intelligible.
b13: after l30, the room holds; one recorded in-breath from Kiran, close and dry, is the last sound before the cut. Do not voice a word or a cut-off 'Mausi'.
music_note: No music for b1 to b3: breath, clinks and the night. From b4 a single low string drone, barely there. It lifts slightly for the lane (b9) and drops back for the call. Under b10 a slow sub pulse like a heartbeat enters; drone and pulse duck right down under l29 and l30. Cut everything to silence on the in-breath in b13, then the question card. Instrumental, no melody, no percussion hits.
ending_question: What will Kiran say: 'Yes, Mausi. He drank it.', which hands Mausi to Aditya, or 'Mausi... the milk has split.', which hands Aditya to Mausi?
writer_notes: S5 English adaptation of script.hi.json (critic round 1 revision), not a literal translation. Read with bible revision 2 (characters.*.voice_note_en, register.english_version, choice) and D-003 direction 7, D-005, D-007, D-008, D-013 and D-014. Same beat ids (b8 and b11 still absent), same line ids (l26 still cut, not reused), same speakers, same order, same silent_seconds and silent_position, same emotion tags in the same places.

Shared picture and sound: on_screen, location, sfx_notes and music_note match the Hindi file. In action, only the quoted cue words are put into English so the English editor can cut on them: b7 'Sneha'; b10 shot 2 runs to 'Don't lie to me.', shot 3 from 'There's mathri', shot 4 through the pause after 'Listen'; the caller-name overlay reads 'Mausi' in the English cut. The b13 sfx note says 'Mausi' for the same reason. The frames themselves do not change.

Locked and anchor lines taken from the bible as written: l29 'Listen... did Damaad ji drink his milk, beta?' (choice.prompt_line.en with characters.mausi's lead-in) and l28 'Did you eat? Don't lie to me. There's mathri in the side pocket of your bag.' (characters.mausi anchor). The drill in l24 quotes the two choice phrases in their bible English form ('He drank it', 'The milk has split'), so a viewer hears the code before Kiran has to use it. Kiran begins neither answer anywhere in the episode.

l05 follows the Hindi revision ('She does Mausi's accounts now'), not the older bible anchor 'She doesn't do weddings any more'. l03 'It'll put me to sleep, though' and l19 'how much puts you to sleep' keep the sleep echo that the Hindi l03 makes with his s1e01 line.

l30 is 'Hello, beta? Did he drink it?' rather than 'Yes, beta?': in English, 'Yes' would be the first word of the A answer ('Yes, Mausi. He drank it.'), and 'Hello' reads as a mother waiting on a silent line. It does not answer ending_question.

Register: Kiran short and blunt with contractions; Aditya in full sentences with few contractions ('I am in no hurry', 'And if it is a lie, I will check the wrist myself', 'You are free to go'); Mausi plain and warm, with beta and Damaad ji kept. Hindi terms kept: Mausi, beta, Damaad ji, mathri. Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: Mausi (MAO-see), Damaad ji (da-MAAD jee), mathri (MUTH-ree), beta (BAY-taa), Rekha (RAY-khaa), Sneha (SNAY-haa), Billu (BIL-loo), Mohit (MO-hit).

Length: 29 lines, about 1,280 characters of English dialogue by hand count (tags excluded), English targets 111.5 s spoken. Add 11 speaker changes at 0.3 s (3.3 s) and 16.4 s of silences for 131.2 s, against the Hindi 132.1 s and the 135 s ceiling. Rates were budgeted at about 12 to 13 characters a second for full lines and 9 to 11 for short or slow ones; all lines sit under the 17 characters a second English subtitle limit (D-014).

Lines off the Hindi length by more than 15%: l14 'Nobody touched Mohit either.' is 3.0 s against 3.6 s (-17%). It is not padded; the slow, quiet read and the l15 shot carry it. All other lines are within about 15% of their Hindi targets.

Gate 0b (26 Nov) measured real eleven_v4 takes 20 to 60% over target_seconds, worst on short and emotional lines. These English targets are hand estimates on the same basis and are likely to run over in the same way. If measured takes push the cut past 135 s, trim in this order: 'Put it down. ' in l04, then 'Listen... ' in l29, then silences; never trim b5, b7, b13, the three outcomes in l24 and l25, l07, l09 or the mathri (same order as the Hindi file).

Tags still to verify in casting: [flatly] on l03, l06 and l13; [hesitant] on l12 and l20; [warmly] on l28, l29 and l30 (fallback [calm]). [sharply] on l04 means low and fast, not loud. l20 'And me?' is a two-word turn and may be unstable on v4: flag it for extra takes rather than padding it. l10 keeps a carrier ('So. Is there a code?') so it is not a bare two-word turn.

l24 uses single quotes round the two code phrases so the subtitle reads them as quoted; the spoken text equals the subtitle text once the tags are removed. If the voice reads the quote marks oddly, drop them in both text and subtitle together.

Not verified: this session had no shell, so the JSON was not machine-parsed and characters and seconds are hand counts, not measurements. Beat ids, line ids, speakers and tag lists were checked against script.hi.json by reading. No line has been voiced.
